clue.text: Expression of surprise following books for the play

indicators.note: following means the exclamation comes after the books in the answer

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the books of the first half of the Bible
hello can be an exclamation of surprise, as in 'hello, what's this?'

explanation.surface: A reader cries out in surprise on finding a play after the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy about the Moor of Venice is one of his best-known plays.

clue.text: A noted publication

parts.note: read as an instrument full of notes, and also a periodical that speaks for a group

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a keyboard instrument that plays notes and a newspaper or journal serving as a mouthpiece.

clue.text: Well! Fancy lathe being seen in hospital yard!

indicators.note: being seen in means the jumbled letters appear between the hospital and yard letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imaginary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at a lathe turning up in a hospital yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well!' looks like an exclamation but is the adjective for being in good health; 'Fancy' is the anagram signal, not a verb of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Well, as an adjective, means in good health.

clue.text: Code number for the fabric

parts.note: a law code is a body of law

explanation.surface: A code number identifies a piece of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn is a fine, light linen or cotton fabric.

clue.text: The position lies precariously to begin the fighting

indicators.note: precariously means in an unstable way, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A general's battle position is shaky as war breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: To open hostilities is the set phrase for starting a war or fight.

clue.text: Die to complete the training

definitions.meaning: in one informal sense, to ... is to die or lose consciousness
a military cadet passes out on finishing training, with a parade

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to die or faint and, in Britain, to graduate from a military training course.

clue.text: Control applied by artist in copper

parts.note: to police something is to control it
John Constable was an English landscape painter

explanation.surface: A painter applies a control technique when working in copper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal an artist works in; it is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is British slang for a police officer, and a constable is the lowest police rank.

clue.text: Indicator of trouble to come before the fall

definitions.text: Indicator of trouble to come before the fall

parts.words: Indicator of trouble to come before the fall
parts.note: a warning sign of trouble ahead, seen before the rain falls

explanation.definitionFit: A dark cloud warns of a coming storm, and figuratively of trouble ahead, before the rain falls.

clue.text: Dope obtained as a symbol held by explorer

indicators.note: held by means the symbol is placed inside the explorer's name

parts.note: Captain Lawrence Oates was an explorer on Scott's Antarctic expedition
pi is the Greek-letter symbol for the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter

explanation.surface: Drugs turn up as a token in an explorer's possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are narcotic drugs derived from opium, and dope is slang for drugs.

clue.text: Shift altered to work by foot

indicators.note: shift means move about, so the letters of altered are rearranged

explanation.surface: A factory shift is altered so that machines are worked by foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the fodder and 'Shift' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To treadle is to operate a machine by a foot pedal, as on an old sewing machine.

clue.text: Broken leg, we hear, could adjust one's speed

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with a broken leg overhears talk of how fast they might move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a sound signal, but it is just anagram fodder with LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed wheel in a gearbox changes the ratio of drive, so it can alter the speed of a vehicle.

clue.text: Girl with bad back after a ball

indicators.note: after places the turned word behind the ball in the answer

parts.note: O is round like a ball

indicators.note: back means the word for bad is read from its end to its start

parts.note: evil means bad

explanation.surface: A girl with a sore back turns up after a ball, the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance, but here it is only the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a girl's first name.

clue.text: The senator's own alliance

indicators.note: the senator's own letters contain the answer, as a possession held within the word

explanation.surface: A senator has a private alliance of his own.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation is a military alliance of Western nations.

clue.text: Machine (not A1, note) tacked badly, totally frustrated

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together in a disordered way
not means the following letters are left out of the word machine

parts.note: A and 1, the figure read as the letter I
n. is the standard abbreviation for a note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: A machine, which is not first-rate, is poorly tacked together and leaves its owner exasperated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A, I and N from MACHINE, leaving MCHE, which is mixed up with TACKED by 'badly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being checkmated in chess means being utterly beaten, with every escape blocked, so it is used for complete frustration.

clue.text: I'm held up by overheads in the theatre

definitions.text: I'm held up by overheads in the theatre

parts.words: I'm held up by overheads in the theatre
parts.note: a stage figure supported by strings from a controller above

explanation.definitionFit: A string puppet is suspended from above by the puppeteer's strings during a theatre show.

clue.text: The way to go round using a permit

parts.note: by means using, as in travelling by train
a pass is a permit allowing entry

explanation.surface: A driver uses a permit to take the road round town.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass is a road built to take traffic around a town rather than through it.

clue.text: Pedal in church the French set in order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
le is French for the

indicators.note: set in order means arranged anew, so the letters of set are reordered

explanation.surface: In church, a French organist puts the pedals in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeste pedal on a piano softens the tone, so the word names that pedal.

clue.text: Butterfly man?

parts.note: not a lepidopterist but the composer of the opera Madama Butterfly

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian composer wrote the opera Madama Butterfly, so he is the man behind it.

clue.text: Calm letter from abroad about high rise turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the whole string is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
C is short for circa, about
an alp is a high mountain, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: A foreign letter about a tower block calms its readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ETA + C + ALP to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate is to calm someone, pacifying their anger.

clue.text: Admit defeat against a good player, say

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a good player is heard, not seen

parts.note: a seed is a highly ranked player in a tournament

explanation.surface: A player facing a top seed admits defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to admit that one has lost.

clue.text: Sweet nothing when one displaces hydrogen

indicators.note: displaces means one letter takes the place of another in the word for nothing

parts.note: nought is zero, nothing
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A chemistry teacher says nothing happens when one atom replaces hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaces' puts A in place of the H of NOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Synthetic account worried Cyril

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters of the name are shaken up

explanation.surface: A synthetic account of events worries a man called Cyril.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a synthetic fibre or resin made from acrylic acid.

clue.text: Make known that an ambassador almost dined

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word for ambassador loses its final letter

parts.note: a nuncio is a papal ambassador
ate means dined

explanation.surface: Someone announces that a diplomat has nearly finished dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To annunciate is to announce or proclaim, making something known.

clue.text: British soldier returning in ship

indicators.note: returning means the soldier's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A British soldier comes home aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted square-rigged sailing ship.

clue.text: The whole taken together is repulsive

definitions.meaning: a ... amount is the total before deductions

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a total amount and also, informally, disgusting.

clue.text: Rich man to the fellows below?

indicators.note: below means the fellows come under to in this down entry

parts.note: taken as written
FF is an abbreviation for fellows

explanation.surface: A rich man looks down on the fellows below him.
explanation.definitionFit: A toff is British slang for an upper-class or wealthy person.

clue.text: 'esitate with time to turn aside

parts.note: hesitate with its h dropped, Cockney style; its synonym haver, to hesitate, drops its h likewise

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks someone to hesitate a moment before turning away.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''esitate' asks for a word meaning hesitate with its H dropped too: HAVER, to dither, becomes AVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert is to turn something away or aside, as in averting your eyes.

clue.text: Big room one left untidy — a mess

indicators.note: untidy means in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A big room that someone has left untidy is a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, complicated situation, a mess.

clue.text: Two of these for a match?

definitions.text: Two of these for a match?

parts.words: Two of these for a match?
parts.note: a football or cricket match needs two sides of that many players each

explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket teams have eleven players each, and are called elevens, so a match needs two.

clue.text: Carries out one's personal belongings

definitions.meaning: to effect something is to bring it about or carry it out
personal ... are the belongings a person owns

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning brings about and a plural noun for personal possessions.
